title: A Micropatterning Assay for Measuring Cell Chirality
protocol: Draw an array of microscale rings using CAD software.
Print a transparency mask of the pattern at the desired resolution.
Conduct ultraviolet (UV) photolithography using the mask containing desired features to make a negative photoresist mold.
Cover a silicon wafer spin-coated with photoresist by the transparency mask.
Polymerize the photoresist under transparent regions of the mask by UV light.
Prepare PDMS elastomeric prepolymers by mixing with its curing agent at a 10:1 ratio.
Cast the mixture onto the mold in a Petri dish.
Place the dish in a vacuum chamber for 30 min to remove air bubbles in PDMS.
Bake the mixture in an oven at 60 °C for at least 2 h.
Cut the pattern arrays into stamps after complete curing of PDMS.
Clean the glass slides.
Soak the slides in a 100% ethanol bath.
Sonicate the slides for 5 min.
Rinse the slides with water.
Repeat soaking in acetone, sonicating for 5 min, and rinsing with water.
Repeat soaking in isopropanol, sonicating for 5 min, and rinsing with water.
Dry the slides using a nitrogen stream.
Place cleaned slides into the evaporation chamber.
Insert gold and titanium crucibles under the shutters.
Pump down the chamber to create a vacuum lower than 10-5 Pa.
Focus the electron beam onto the metal.
Adjust the power for an appropriate depositing rate.
Open the shutter to start titanium deposition.
Close the shutter when reaching a thickness of 15 Å.
Switch crucibles and begin gold deposition after cooling.
Focus the electron beam on the gold metal.
Adjust the power for an appropriate depositing rate.
Open the shutter to start gold deposition.
Close the shutter when reaching a thickness of 150 Å.
Vent the chamber.
Remove the gold-coated glass slides from the evaporation chamber.
Cut the titanium/gold-coated slide into smaller pieces, if desired.
Soak the slides in 100% ethanol for at least 10 min on an orbital shaker with the gold side up.
Aspirate out the ethanol.
Dry each slide by blowing with a nitrogen stream.
Clean the PDMS stamps with soapy water.
Rinse the PDMS stamps with 100% ethanol.
Dry the PDMS stamps with nitrogen gas.
Dissolve 5.74 mg of octadecanethiol (C18) powder in 10 mL of 100% ethanol to prepare a 2 mM C18 solution.
Seal and store the C18 solution at room temperature.
Soak the PDMS stamps in the C18 solution with the patterned surface facing down for 10 seconds.
Gently dry the PDMS stamp with nitrogen gas for 60 seconds, placing the stream away from the stamp first until most liquid is evaporated and then moving closer to fully dry the stamp.
Lay the stamp face down onto gold slides for 60 seconds before removal.
Gently tap the tweezers on the stamps to ensure proper transfer of patterns without pushing too hard.
Visual inspect the stamp during tapping to ensure uniform contact with the glass slide.
Pipette 1 mL of 70% ethanol into an inverted Petri dish lid.
Lay down a piece of parafilm onto the surface, covering it completely and ensuring no air bubbles are present.
Remove excess ethanol if necessary.
Prepare a 2 mM HS-(CH2)11-EG3-OH (EG3) solution by diluting 5 µL stock solution in 5 mL of 100% ethanol.
Store the diluted EG3 solution at 4 °C and undiluted EG3 stock at -20 °C.
Micropipette 40 µL droplets of EG3 onto parafilm in a humidity chamber for each quarter glass slide.
Use tweezers to place C18-printed gold slides face down onto the EG3 droplets on the parafilm, ensuring no bubbles are present under the slides.
Gently push the gold slides together without lifting them to minimize evaporation and ensure proper contact with the EG3 solution.
Seal the Petri dish tightly with parafilm and leave it at room temperature for at least 3 h.
If extensive incubation is desired, double seal the Petri dish and leave it for up to 24 h.
In a biosafety cabinet, place gold slides face up in a Petri dish.
Soak and rinse the gold slides three times in 70% ethanol to remove EG3.
Leave the gold slides in 70% ethanol for 10 min for sterilization.
Aspirate out the ethanol from the Petri dish.
Replace the ethanol with sterile PBS.
Add 4-5 mL of PBS to lay down parafilm and remove bubbles.
Aspirate out the excess PBS.
Prepare a 50 µg/mL fibronectin solution in sterile PBS.
Micropipette 50 µL droplets of fibronectin solution for each quarter slide onto the parafilm.
Place slides face down onto the droplets using wafer tweezers to ensure no bubbles under the slides.
Gently push the slides together without lifting them.
Leave the Petri dish in the biosafety cabinet for 30 min.
Rinse fibronectin-patterned slides three times with PBS after 30 min.
Store fibronectin-patterned slides in PBS at 4 °C for about a month.
Warm up cell culture media and trypsin in a 37 °C water bath.
(Optional) Soak patterned slides in culture media in a 12-well plate, warm up to 37 °C in an incubator prior to trypsinization of cells.
Trypsinize the cells.
Neutralize with FBS-containing media.
Centrifuge down at 100 x g for 3 min.
Resuspend by mixing well with fresh media.
Count the cells and dilute to 200,000 cells/mL.
Add 0.5 mL of cell suspension to each well containing one gold slide.
Gently shake the well plate for uniform cell seeding.
Store the well plate in an incubator for 15 min to allow for cell attachment.
Check cell attachment under a microscope after 15 minutes and allow additional time if needed.
Aspirate out media containing unattached cells from each well.
Add 1 mL of culture media to each well.
Supplement additional reagents to the culture media at this step for drug treatment.
Culture the cells in an incubator for 24 h and check confluency to determine chirality formation.
Fix cells upon reaching confluence by removing culture media, rinsing once with PBS, and adding 4% paraformaldehyde solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min and rinse three times with PBS.
Image each ring on the slides using a phase-contrast microscope with camera functionality.
Download MATLAB code files from supplementary files.
Add code folder and sub-folders with circular statistics toolbox to MATLAB path.
Open "ROI_selection.m" file in MATLAB.
Change directory to desired data folder in line 4 of "ROI_selection.m".
Adjust inner circle size of the ring in line 14 of "ROI_selection.m".
Adjust outer circle size of the ring in line 14 of "ROI_selection.m".
Run "ROI_selection.m" to determine ROI in phase-contrast images.
Manually drag selection square to fit the ring.
Double-click on image to confirm ROI selection.
Repeat for every image in folder until all ROIs are selected.
Open "Analysis_batch.m" file.
Change directory to the folder specified in step 6.2.
For Windows users, switch "/" into "\" in lines 5, 6, 124, and 130.
Click on the Run button to execute the code "Analysis_batch.m".
The execution will generate a "datatoexcel.txt" file containing circular statistics for each ring and the numbers of clockwise, non-chiral, and anti-clockwise rings.
